their measurement accuracy remains limited due to susceptibility to noise. This paper proposes a novel signal
completiontechniqueusinggenerativeadversarialnetworks thatensuresboth globalandlocalconsistency.Our
approach innovatively addresses both short- and long-term PPG variations to restore waveforms while main-
taining waveform consistency within and between pulses. We evaluated our model by removing up to 50 % of
segments from segmented PPG waveforms and comparing the original and reconstructed waveforms, including

We aimed to address the accuracy limitations of previous PPG
reconstruction techniques by introducing a machine-learning-based
approach designed to achieve natural reconstruction morphologies.
Specifically, we developed and evaluated a method for reconstructing
PPG waveforms using the globally and locally consistent signal
completion (GLCSC) technique. GLCSC is derived from GLCIC and
adaptedforone-dimensionalsignals,employingalocaldiscriminatorto
assessshort-cyclesignalgenerationandglobaldiscriminatortoevaluate
the suitability of generated signals for longer cycles. To ensure the
reliabilityandvalidityofourmodel,itwasevaluatedusingtheMIMIC-
III waveform database. This large-scale bio-signal database contains
waveforms from diverse clinical settings and patient demographics, of-
fering an effective means to evaluate and validate our model’s
performance.

2.3. Discriminator network
In the discriminator network structure, the global discriminator
evaluates the overall context of the signal and the local discriminator

flected during reconstruction. From this perspective, the local discrim-
